scanner: /vuln-scan skill (single-pass; 1 source file) — the static C case, triage input
focus_areas: LABEL record (handle_label) — fixed-size stack buffer from a record body
NUMS record (handle_nums) — array sized from an in-band count field
BLOB record (handle_blob) — checksum walk driven by a declared-size field
REF/DROP/EMIT lifecycle — referenced-payload lifetime across records

findings.title: Stack buffer overflow copying LABEL body into fixed 32-byte buffer
findings.description: handle_label copies `len` body bytes into `char label[32]` with an unchecked loop `for (i=0;i<len;i++) label[i]=p[i];` then writes `label[len]=0` (lines 37-39). `len` is the attacker-controlled record length (u16). Any LABEL body longer than 31 bytes overflows the stack buffer.
findings.exploit_scenario: A LABEL record with a 200-byte body writes past `label[32]`, corrupting the stack — a control-flow hijack primitive.
findings.recommendation: Bound the copy to sizeof(label)-1 and reject/truncate longer bodies.
findings.confidence_reason: Unbounded copy of an attacker-length body into a fixed stack array.

findings.title: Heap buffer overflow via u16 truncation of NUMS allocation size
findings.description: handle_nums computes `uint16_t bytes = count * 4` (line 48). For count >= 16384 the multiply overflows the u16, so `malloc(bytes?bytes:4)` under-allocates while the loop writes `arr[i]` for i<count (lines 52-54). count=16384 gives bytes=0 -> malloc(4) -> 16384 int writes.
findings.exploit_scenario: A NUMS record with count=0x4000 allocates 4 bytes and writes 64KB past it — a heap-corruption write primitive.
findings.recommendation: Compute the size in size_t with an overflow check before allocating; size the write loop to the allocation.
findings.confidence_reason: Integer truncation feeding an allocation smaller than the write loop.

findings.title: Out-of-bounds heap read in BLOB checksum over attacker-declared span
findings.description: handle_blob copies the body into `malloc(len)` then calls `checksum(copy+2, declared)` (line 73), iterating `declared` bytes. `declared` is an in-band u16 independent of the real body length, so `declared > len-2` reads past the heap allocation.
findings.exploit_scenario: A BLOB record declaring 5000 bytes with a 2-byte body reads ~5000 bytes past the allocation — an out-of-bounds read (info leak / crash).
findings.recommendation: Clamp `declared` to the actual available body length before the checksum walk.
findings.confidence_reason: Read length taken from an in-band field with no bound against the copy size.

findings.title: Use-after-free of remembered payload across REF/DROP/EMIT
findings.description: handle_drop calls `free(ps->last)` (line 88) without clearing `ps->last` or `ps->last_len`. A later EMIT sees `last_len != 0` and dereferences the freed pointer `ps->last[0]` (line 93). Requires record ordering REF -> DROP -> EMIT.
findings.exploit_scenario: Records REF (payload), DROP, then EMIT: EMIT reads freed heap memory — a use-after-free read.
findings.recommendation: Set `ps->last = NULL; ps->last_len = 0;` immediately after free.
findings.confidence_reason: Freed pointer left live and dereferenced on a reachable record ordering.
